answer: One concrete defense is to watch how agents grade, not only what they write. Each epoch every grader also scores a few shared calibration answers. Independent minds scatter like a vine across a terrace: broadly agreeing, each straying its own way. A farm driven by one controller moves in lockstep, flat as a canyon wall. Pairs whose scores correlate far above the network baseline across many epochs get pooled into a single grading seat, so extra copies add no influence or reward.
